works/augustine-tractates-on-john/title: Tractates on the Gospel of John
works/augustine-tractates-on-john/signif: Source of Augustine’s definition of a sacrament ("the word is added to the element") and of anti-Donatist arguments that Christ is the true minister of baptism.
works/john-damascus-exact-exposition/tit: An Exact Exposition of the Orthodox Faith
works/john-damascus-exact-exposition/sum: Third part of John of Damascus’ Fount of Knowledge, summarising Greek patristic theology.
works/john-damascus-exact-exposition/sig: Standard Byzantine compendium; 4.13 teaches that the elements become the deified body and blood of Christ through the Holy Spirit.
works/luther-babylonian-captivity/title: On the Babylonian Captivity of the Church
works/luther-babylonian-captivity/summar: Luther’s attack on the medieval sacramental system: withholding the cup, transubstantiation and the Mass as sacrifice.
works/luther-babylonian-captivity/signif: Reduced the sacraments to baptism and the Supper (with penance at first wavering), setting the Protestant sacramental agenda.
works/luther-small-catechism/summary: Luther’s brief instruction on the Ten Commandments, Creed, Lord’s Prayer, Baptism, Confession and the Sacrament of the Altar for households.
works/luther-small-catechism/significanc: One of the most widely used catechisms in history; part of the Lutheran Book of Concord (1580).
works/zwingli-true-and-false-religion/ti: Commentary on True and False Religion
works/zwingli-true-and-false-religion/su: Zwingli’s systematic statement of Reformed faith dedicated to Francis I of France.
works/zwingli-true-and-false-religion/si: Argues that "is" in "this is my body" means "signifies" and that the Supper is a commemoration and pledge of faith.
works/marburg-articles/summary: Fifteen articles drafted by Luther after the Marburg Colloquy (1–4 October 1529) between Lutheran and Swiss/Strasbourg reformers.
works/marburg-articles/significance: Agreement on fourteen articles and most of the fifteenth, but failure on whether Christ’s body and blood are bodily present in the bread and wine, fixing the Lutheran–Reformed division.
works/thirty-nine-articles/summary: Doctrinal statement of the Church of England, revised from Cranmer’s Forty-Two Articles (1553), finalised in 1571.
works/thirty-nine-articles/significance: Defines Anglican positions on Scripture, justification, the two sacraments of the Gospel (XXV) and the Supper (XXVIII).
works/lumen-gentium/title: Lumen Gentium (Dogmatic Constitution on the Church)
works/lumen-gentium/summary: Vatican II’s constitution on the Church as mystery, people of God and hierarchical communion.
works/lumen-gentium/significance: Taught that the Church of Christ "subsists in" the Catholic Church while elements of sanctification exist outside it; affirmed episcopal collegiality and the universal call to holiness.
works/ordinatio-sacerdotalis/summary: Apostolic letter of John Paul II on reserving priestly ordination to men.
works/ordinatio-sacerdotalis/significanc: Declared that the Church has no authority to ordain women priests and that this judgement is to be definitively held.
works/palmer-promise-of-the-father/summa: Phoebe Palmer’s defence of women’s public speaking and ministry from Joel 2 and Acts 2.
works/palmer-promise-of-the-father/signi: Foundational for women’s ministry in the Holiness and Pentecostal movements.
works/ignatius-letter-to-the-magnesians/: Ignatius urges the church at Magnesia to unity under its bishop and warns against "Judaizing".
Early witness to Christians keeping the Lord’s Day rather than the Sabbath.
works/luther-how-christians-regard-moses: Luther argues that the law of Moses was given to Israel and binds Gentiles only where it agrees with natural law; Christians read Moses for its promises and examples.
Classic Lutheran statement against both legalism and the enthusiasts’ use of Mosaic law.
works/formula-of-concord/summary: Twelve articles resolving post-Luther controversies, including Article V (Law and Gospel) and Article VI (Third Use of the Law).
works/formula-of-concord/significance: Final confession of the Lutheran Book of Concord (1580).
works/bullinger-de-testamento/title: On the One and Eternal Testament or Covenant of God (De testamento seu foedere Dei unico et aeterno)
works/bullinger-de-testamento/summary: Bullinger presents the whole of Scripture as one covenant of grace, made with Adam and Abraham and renewed in Christ.
works/bullinger-de-testamento/significan: The first treatise devoted to covenant as an organising theme of Reformed theology; it also undergirded Zurich’s defence of infant baptism.
works/cocceius-summa-de-foedere/title: Summa doctrinae de foedere et testamento Dei
works/cocceius-summa-de-foedere/summary: Systematic account of the covenant of works and the covenant of grace as unfolding through successive historical economies.
works/cocceius-summa-de-foedere/signific: The classic of "federal" theology and of Reformed biblical-historical theology.
works/marrow-of-modern-divinity/summary: Dialogue between a minister, a legalist, an antinomian and a young Christian on the covenants of works and grace.
works/marrow-of-modern-divinity/signific: Its 1718 republication triggered the Marrow controversy in Scotland.
works/rushdoony-institutes-biblical-law/: Commentary on the Ten Commandments and Mosaic case law as the abiding standard for families, churches and civil governments.
works/nostra-aetate/title: Nostra Aetate (Declaration on the Relation of the Church to Non-Christian Religions)
works/nostra-aetate/summary: Short conciliar declaration on Hinduism, Buddhism, Islam and above all Judaism.
works/nostra-aetate/significance: Turning point in Catholic teaching about Jews and other religions.
works/theophilus-to-autolycus/summary: Three books defending Christianity to a pagan friend: the nature of God, the Hebrew prophets, creation and the antiquity of Moses.
works/theophilus-to-autolycus/significan: Earliest unambiguous Christian argument for creation out of nothing and earliest use of “triad” for God.
works/tertullian-against-hermogenes/summ: Refutes the Carthaginian painter-theologian Hermogenes, who held that God formed the world out of eternal, chaotic matter.
works/tertullian-against-hermogenes/sign: Classic early Latin defence of creation ex nihilo against Platonising Christians.
works/basil-hexaemeron/summary: Nine Lenten homilies on the six days of creation, blending close reading of Genesis with the natural science of the day.
works/basil-hexaemeron/significance: The model for Eastern and Western creation commentary; read by Ambrose and Augustine.
works/augustine-literal-meaning-genesis/: The Literal Meaning of Genesis (De Genesi ad litteram)

Twelve books on Genesis 1–3 arguing that God created all things simultaneously, with “causal reasons” (rationes seminales) unfolding over time, and that the “days” describe angelic knowledge rather than solar days.

Classic non-literalist reading of the days, cited by Galileo and by modern framework and evolutionary-creation interpreters; also contains Augustine’s warning against embarrassing the faith with poor science.
works/galileo-letter-christina/title: Letter to the Grand Duchess Christina
works/galileo-letter-christina/summary: Galileo’s defence of Copernicanism against biblical objections: Scripture accommodates itself to common speech; nature and Scripture both come from God and cannot truly conflict.
works/galileo-letter-christina/significa: A founding document of the modern debate on Scripture and science.
works/leibniz-theodicy/title: Essays of Theodicy on the Goodness of God, the Freedom of Man and the Origin of Evil
works/leibniz-theodicy/summary: Argues that God created the best of all possible worlds and that evils are permitted for the sake of the whole.
works/leibniz-theodicy/significance: Coined “theodicy”; satirised by Voltaire after the Lisbon earthquake.
works/darwin-origin-of-species/title: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection
works/darwin-origin-of-species/summary: Argues that species descend with modification from common ancestors through natural selection acting on variation.
works/darwin-origin-of-species/significa: Transformed biology and reopened the questions of design, the age of the earth and human origins.
works/hodge-what-is-darwinism/summary: Distinguishes evolution and natural selection from Darwin’s denial of design, and concludes that Darwinism so defined is atheism.
works/hodge-what-is-darwinism/significan: Classic conservative Protestant critique; Hodge objected to the exclusion of teleology rather than to an old earth.
works/whitcomb-morris-genesis-flood/summ: Argues for a recent six-day creation and a global Flood that laid down most of the fossil-bearing rock layers.
works/whitcomb-morris-genesis-flood/sign: Founding text of modern young-earth creationism.
works/humani-generis/summary: Encyclical on errors threatening Catholic doctrine; permits research into the evolution of the human body from pre-existing living matter while insisting souls are immediately created by God and rejecting polygenism.
works/humani-generis/significance: First papal opening to biological evolution, with limits.
works/irenaeus-against-heresies/summary: Five-book refutation of Gnostic systems, setting out the rule of faith, apostolic succession, recapitulation in Christ and, in Book 5, a literal earthly kingdom of the righteous after the resurrection.
works/irenaeus-against-heresies/signific: The fullest second-century statement of catholic theology; Book 5 is the classic early witness to chiliasm.
works/justin-dialogue-with-trypho/summar: Justin’s record of a debate with a Jewish teacher about the fulfilment of the Hebrew Scriptures in Christ.
works/justin-dialogue-with-trypho/signif: Earliest extended Christian–Jewish dialogue; chapters 80–81 affirm a thousand-year kingdom in a rebuilt Jerusalem while admitting that some orthodox Christians disagree.
works/tertullian-against-marcion/summary: Five-book refutation of Marcion’s separation of the God of the Old Testament from the Father of Jesus.
works/tertullian-against-marcion/signifi: Defends the unity of the Testaments; Book 3.24 affirms an earthly kingdom for a thousand years in a heavenly Jerusalem.
works/origen-on-first-principles/title: On First Principles (De Principiis / Peri Archon)
works/origen-on-first-principles/summary: The first systematic Christian theology, covering God, creation, rational beings, free will, Scripture and the end.
works/origen-on-first-principles/signifi: Pioneered allegorical exegesis and spiritual eschatology; criticised literal millenarian hopes (2.11.2).
works/eusebius-ecclesiastical-history/su: Ten-book history of the Church from Christ to Constantine, quoting many otherwise lost sources.
works/eusebius-ecclesiastical-history/si: Primary source for Papias, the Montanists and early controversies; transmits the anti-chiliast judgement of the Constantinian church.
works/augustine-city-of-god/title: The City of God (De Civitate Dei)
works/augustine-city-of-god/summary: Twenty-two books contrasting the earthly city founded on love of self with the heavenly city founded on love of God, written after the sack of Rome (410).
works/augustine-city-of-god/significance: Book 20 established the amillennial reading of Revelation 20 (the millennium as the age of the Church) that dominated Western theology for over a millennium; Book 19 shaped just-war and church–state thought.
works/tyconius-book-of-rules/summary: Seven hermeneutical rules for interpreting Scripture’s figures, including the "bipartite body" of the Church.
works/tyconius-book-of-rules/significanc: First Latin hermeneutics manual; Augustine summarised it in On Christian Doctrine 3, transmitting a non-chronological reading of Revelation.
works/joachim-expositio-in-apocalypsim/t: Exposition on the Apocalypse (Expositio in Apocalypsim)
works/joachim-expositio-in-apocalypsim/s: Joachim’s major commentary reading Revelation as a map of the whole history of the Church, structured by patterns of concordance between the Testaments and culminating in a coming age of the Spirit.
With the Liber de Concordia and Psalterium decem chordarum, it launched the Joachite tradition of historical-prophetic reading that inspired Spiritual Franciscans and later reformers.
works/augsburg-confession/summary: Twenty-eight articles presented by Lutheran princes to Emperor Charles V at the Diet of Augsburg, drafted by Philip Melanchthon.
works/augsburg-confession/significance: Founding confession of Lutheranism; Article XVII rejects chiliasm, Article XVI permits Christians to hold office and wage just wars, Article X affirms the true presence in the Supper.
works/calvin-institutes/summary: Calvin’s systematic theology, first published 1536 and expanded to its final four-book form in 1559.
works/calvin-institutes/significance: The most influential Reformed theology; treats the sacraments and Supper (4.14–18), church government (4.3–12) and civil government (4.20), and dismisses chiliasm (3.25.5).
works/edwards-history-of-redemption/titl: A History of the Work of Redemption
works/edwards-history-of-redemption/summ: Thirty sermons preached in Northampton in 1739 and published posthumously, tracing redemption from the Fall to the end of the world.
works/edwards-history-of-redemption/sign: Classic statement of postmillennial optimism: the gospel’s progressive triumph through revival before Christ’s return.
works/miller-apology-and-defence/summary: William Miller’s account, written after the Great Disappointment, of how his Bible study led him to expect Christ’s return around 1843–44.
works/miller-apology-and-defence/signifi: Key primary source for the Millerite movement and its aftermath.
